title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement_short: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays. The overall run time complexity should be O(log (m+n)).
constraints: nums1.length == m, nums2.length == n, 0 <= m <= 1000, 0 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m + n <= 2000, -10^6 <= nums1[i], nums2[j] <= 10^6
hint: Strict O(log(m+n)) runtime complexity on two sorted arrays requires binary searching the partition position on the smaller array.
keywords: median of the two sorted arrays
why_not: Right: Binary Search partitions the smaller array such that left combined elements equal right combined elements in O(log(min(m, n))) time. Not Two Pointers: Merging arrays with two pointers takes O(m + n) time, violating the O(log(m+n)) mandate. Not Sorting: Concatenating and re-sorting costs O((m+n) log(m+n)) time and extra memory. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Maintaining min/max heaps takes O((m+n) log(m+n)) time.
